detailed_description: World Clock shows current time across the built-in city list directly in the browser. The page starts with New York, London, Tokyo, and Shanghai, and the selector lets you add any remaining built-in city that is not already shown. Each card displays the city name, current time, short date, computed UTC offset, and a day or night indicator based on the local hour. You can switch between 12-hour and 24-hour display and choose whether seconds are visible. The tool is meant for quick timezone reference; it does not schedule meetings, sync calendars, or include a global city database beyond the current list.
usage_steps: Open the World Clock tool page
Default display shows New York, London, Tokyo, and Shanghai
Select one of the remaining built-in cities from the dropdown menu
Click 'Add City' button to add it to the display
Click the × on a city card to remove it
Use top options to toggle 24-hour format or show seconds
usage_examples: Check the current time in New York, London, Tokyo, and Shanghai.
Compare work hours before messaging a teammate in another timezone.
Switch to 12-hour display when sharing a time with a US-based contact.
Hide seconds when you only need a calmer reference clock.

faqs.question: Which cities are supported?
faqs.answer: The current built-in list includes New York, London, Tokyo, and Shanghai.

faqs.question: Is the time accurate?
faqs.answer: The time is based on your device's system time and updates every second. As long as your device time is accurate, the displayed city times will be accurate.

faqs.question: How do I know if it's day or night?
faqs.answer: Each city card shows a sun ☀️ or moon 🌙 icon. Sun indicates daytime (6:00-18:00), moon indicates nighttime (other hours).

faqs.question: Can it schedule meetings or export calendar events?
faqs.answer: No. It is a display tool for current times only; use a calendar app for invites and timezone-safe scheduling.

faqs.question: What should I check before relying on it?
faqs.answer: Confirm your device time is correct and double-check dates around daylight-saving changes or cross-date meetings.
